raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer:*

I'm 66. Been working this land since I was a boy. Me and my old lady, that's it — the kids are grown and gone to the city. 14 mu 5 fen, all in wheat and maize, year after year. Don't know any other way.

I don't read. Never went to school. What I know is what my father taught me and what I've seen work on this ground for fifty years. The fellow from the extension station comes through sometimes talking about rates and whatnot, but I just nod. I do what I do.

**Wheat** — I put it in around the 10th of October. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the shop in town. Come spring after the wheat greens up, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Water it at sowing, again in spring when it's warming, and at jointing. If the ears are filling and it's dry I'll give it one more. Three, maybe four waterings. The well costs money to run so I don't waste it. Harvest in early June — hire the combine, everyone does.

**Maize** — soon as the wheat's off, within the week. The tractor man comes and rotary-tills, then we drill the seed same day. Have to move fast or you lose days. Maize doesn't need much fertilizer from me because the wheat stubble feeds it some — I just put down one bag of urea per mu and that's it. Usually don't irrigate unless July is bone dry. Harvest end of September.

**Pests and weeds** — I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring, have to, otherwise the weeds take over. Bugs I only spray if I see them. Money doesn't grow on trees.

**The money** — seeds and fertilizer come out of cash. Wheat seed I sometimes save from last year if the grain looked good. Maize seed you have to buy, the hybrid kind, can't save it. Most of my cost goes to the machinery fellows — plowing, combining, all that.

**What I expect** — 800-900 jin of wheat per mu is a good year. Maize about 1000 jin. If the sky cooperates, a bit more. If not, less. Been doing this long enough I don't get worked up about it.
